title: Finitely generated kernels stabilize in a directed system of module localizations
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $D_i$ commutative rings with ring maps $d_{ji}:D_i\to D_j$ for $i\le j$, and $P_i$ $D_i$-modules with additive maps $p_{ji}:P_i\to P_j$ satisfying $p_{ji}(ax)=d_{ji}(a)p_{ji}(x)$. The ring and module transitions are identities at equal indices and compatible with composition. Let $P$ be an abelian group with compatible $D_i$-module structures, meaning that its $D_i$-action is the restriction of its $D_j$-action along $d_{ji}$ for $i\le j$. Let $\psi_i:P_i\to P$ be $D_i$-linear maps with $\psi_jp_{ji}=\psi_i$, exhibiting $P$ as the colimit of the underlying abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose for every $i\le j$ there is a multiplicative subset $W_{ji}\subset D_i$ such that $d_{ji}$ exhibits $D_j$ as $W_{ji}^{-1}D_i$ and the canonical $D_j$-linear map $W_{ji}^{-1}P_i\to P_j$, $x/w\mapsto d_{ji}(w)^{-1}p_{ji}(x)$, is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and assume that $\ker(\psi_{i_0})$ is a finitely generated $D_{i_0}$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then there is $j\ge i_0$ such that $\psi_l:P_l\to P$ is injective for every $l\ge j$. No Noetherianity or finite generation of $P_i$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $K=\ker(\psi_{i_0})$. By finite generation choose $z_1,\ldots,z_r\in K$ generating $K$ over $D_{i_0}$. Regard the underlying abelian groups $P_i$ and $P$ as $\mathbf Z$-modules. Additive maps are exactly $\mathbf Z$-linear maps, so the assumed abelian-group colimit is also their module colimit. Apply the vanishing clause of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] separately to $\psi_{i_0}(z_a)=0$: for each $a$ obtain $j_a\ge i_0$ with $p_{j_ai_0}(z_a)=0$. The index category is small and filtered because $I$ is small, nonempty and directed, as required.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), middle proof paragraph; Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit) for eventual vanishing; Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module) for fractions

proof.text: Choose a common upper bound $j$ of $i_0,j_1,\ldots,j_r$ by repeatedly applying directedness; if $r=0$, take $j=i_0$. For any $l\ge j$, composition compatibility gives $p_{li_0}(z_a)=p_{lj_a}(p_{j_ai_0}(z_a))=0$. For $y\in K$, write $y=\sum_a b_a z_a$ with $b_a\in D_{i_0}$ using [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Additivity and semilinearity give $p_{li_0}(y)=\sum_a d_{li_0}(b_a)p_{li_0}(z_a)=0$. Thus one $j$ kills the whole initial kernel at every later stage.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), middle proof paragraph; Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit) for eventual vanishing; Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module) for fractions

proof.text: Fix $l\ge j$ and $x\in P_l$ with $\psi_l(x)=0$. Apply the assumed isomorphism $W_{li_0}^{-1}P_{i_0}\cong P_l$. By the fraction construction in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], its preimage has the form $y/w$ with $y\in P_{i_0}$ and $w\in W_{li_0}$. The stipulated formula for the isomorphism gives $x=d_{li_0}(w)^{-1}p_{li_0}(y)$, hence $p_{li_0}(y)=d_{li_0}(w)x$. Here $d_{li_0}(w)$ is a unit of $D_l$ by the ring-localization hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), middle proof paragraph; Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit) for eventual vanishing; Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module) for fractions

proof.text: Apply the actual cocone and linearity identities to the equation of Step 3: $\psi_{i_0}(y)=\psi_l(p_{li_0}(y))=\psi_l(d_{li_0}(w)x)=d_{li_0}(w)\psi_l(x)=0$, where the scalar action on the last two expressions is the given $D_l$-action on $P$. Therefore $y\in K$. Step 2 gives $p_{li_0}(y)=0$, and Step 3 gives $x=d_{li_0}(w)^{-1}0=0$. Thus $\ker\psi_l=0$. Since $\psi_l$ is additive, $\psi_l(x_1)=\psi_l(x_2)$ implies $\psi_l(x_1-x_2)=0$ and then $x_1=x_2$, proving injectivity for every $l\ge j$. Only invertibility of localization denominators is used; no nonzerodivisor assumption is needed.
